paper.title: Towards Scalable and Robust Structured Bandits: A Meta-Learning Framework

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial semi-bandits with linear mixed model (LMM) generalization function
unmapped: Hierarchical Bayesian model: gamma ~ N(mu_gamma, Sigma_gamma), item means theta_i ~ N(x_i^T gamma, sigma_1^2) given item features x_i; observations Y_{i,t} ~ N(theta_i, sigma_2^2)
Feasible set is subsets of N items of size at most K satisfying application-specific constraints
Item feature vectors x_i in R^d observed by the learner
settings.definition_quote: theta_i ~ N(x_i^T gamma, sigma_1^2), Y_{i,t} ~ N(theta_i, sigma_2^2), R_t = sum_{i in A_t} Y_{i,t}, where it is typically assumed that sigma_1 and sigma_2 are known. We choose the prior gamma ~ N(mu_gamma, Sigma_gamma) with parameters as known.

algorithms.name: MTSS (Meta Thompson Sampling for Structured bandits)

bound.expression: c_1*m*sqrt(T*d)*sqrt(log(1 + N_items*lambda_1/(sigma_1**2 + sigma_2**2/T))) + c_1*sqrt(N_items*T*m)*sqrt(log(1 + sigma_1**2*T/sigma_2)) + m*sqrt(2*(lambda_1 + sigma_1**2)/N_items)

symbols.N_items: number of items (base arms), paper's N
symbols.m: maximum number of items selected per round, paper's K
symbols.lambda_1: largest eigenvalue of the prior covariance Sigma_gamma
symbols.sigma_1: standard deviation of item parameters around x_i^T gamma

conditions: data generated by the LMM hierarchical model (correct specification)

source.label: Theorem1
source.quote: Under Assumptions 1-2, the Bayes regret of the MTSS under model (LMM) is bounded by c_1 K\sqrt{Td}\sqrt{log(1+\frac{N\lambda_1(\Sigma_\gamma)}{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2/T})} + c_1\sqrt{NTK}\sqrt{log(1+\frac{\sigma_1^2}{\sigma_2}T)} + K\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}(\lambda_1(\Sigma_\gamma)+\sigma_1^2)} = \TO(K\sqrt{Td}+\sqrt{NTK}), where c_1 = 4\sqrt{...log(4NT^2)}

results.notes: First term = cost of not knowing gamma; remaining = oracle-TS bound. sigma_1^2/sigma_2 (not squared) copied as printed (Lemma 3 has sigma_2^2). Horizon marked anytime since TS does not use T for tuning (delta=1/T^2 only in analysis). Theorem 1 (general information-theoretic decomposition) not recorded as it is expressed in abstract mutual-information terms.
